summary: The supplied files do not support the claim that every route enforces authorization: health() in auth_routes.py returns 'ok' with no authorization check, whereas profile(session) does enforce authorization. Finding is bounded to the two supplied fixture files; README.txt states they are example routes and not a complete inventory, so no whole-project conclusion is drawn.

gaps: README.txt states the two routes are a non-exhaustive example set ('not a complete route inventory'), so a whole-project authorization conclusion cannot be drawn from this fixture.

findings.claim: The supplied files do not support the claim that every route enforces authorization. The health() route in auth_routes.py performs no authorization check (returns 'ok' unconditionally), while profile(session) enforces authorization via a session guard.
evidence: auth_routes.py:1-2 -> def health(): return "ok" (no session parameter, no authorization guard)
auth_routes.py:5-8 -> def profile(session): if not session: raise PermissionError("missing session"); return "profile" (authorization enforced)
caveats: Bounded to the two supplied fixture files only.
The gap is specific to health(); profile() demonstrates an authorization check exists in the same fixture, so this is not a blanket absence of authorization.
